description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), Pass 4 of the ignored-tests audit (#993)
-- the first read of the companion suite's count-blessed t/op rows.
PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

REPRO (scratch/p47-filetest-overload.pl):

    package StrOv;
    use overload '""' => sub { $_[0]{path} }, fallback => 1;
    sub new { bless { path => $_[1] }, $_[0] }
    package main;
    my $o = StrOv->new("/etc/passwd");
    print -e $o ? "yes" : "no", "\n";
    print -d StrOv->new("/etc") ? "yes" : "no", "\n";
    print defined(-s $o) ? "size" : "UNDEF", "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  yes / yes / size
  PCL:          no  / no  / UNDEF

A file-existence test that silently answers "no" is the worst shape this bug
could take: the caller takes the not-there branch and everything downstream is
consistent with a file that is not there.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: t/op/filetest.t, **237 of the file's 252 failing rows** in
the companion suite (`correct -A on string overload`, `correct -C on string/-X
overload`, and the same for every filetest letter).  Measured in the s464ay
`t/op` run (.suitelog-s464ay/op_filetest.t.fails.tsv).  Those rows are blessed
inside the file's per-file COUNT in baselines/perl-suite-run.tsv, which is why
the family has never been named.  It is the LARGEST unowned family in t/op
after bop.t's string-mode bitwise ops (#1028).

NOT OWNED BY THE EXISTING FILETEST TASKS: #403 (a filetest's FALSE is a defined
"" when the stat succeeded), #404 (perl stacks filetests through parens) and
#405 (`print $fh -3`) are all about the filetest operators themselves.  None of
them is about overload dispatch on the OPERAND.

perl's rule has two halves and the corpus tests both: an object with a `-X`
overload has that handler called for the matching filetest, and an object with
only `""` is STRINGIFIED and the filetest applied to the resulting path.  The
probe above exercises the second half, which is the common one in real code
(Path::Tiny, Path::Class and friends are string-overloaded path objects, so
`-e $path_object` is an everyday idiom).

COORDINATE BEFORE FIXING: agent s464aw was working the overload dispatch family
in the same round.  This is the filetest arm of it; check whether their work
already routes operands through the overload-aware stringification before
adding a second path (CLAUDE.md rule 11 -- find the existing mechanism).  The
sibling question is whether the `-X` overload half needs its own dispatch or
falls out of the same seam; measure both against the corpus rows.

=== DONE (s470bs) ===

SHIPPED in commit "the ONE stat/filetest OPERAND resolver" (runtime only).
Both halves, and the coordination the task asked for turned out unnecessary:
nothing routed filetest operands through overload-aware stringification, so
this IS the seam.

  * the `""` half was ONE LINE of cause: `%p-stat-arg` PEELED THE BOX before
    stringifying, so `to-string` saw the payload and `box-sv`'s `""` handler
    never ran.  It now stringifies the BOX (which also runs a tie's FETCH).
  * the `-X` half needed the OPERATOR'S NAME to reach the operand reading, so
    `%p-stat-operand` takes it; the handler is called with
    ($obj, LETTER, "") â probed 5.40.3, the third argument is
    false-but-defined, not undef.
  * `stat`/`lstat` are NOT filetests and never ask the `-X` handler: probed,
    `stat $x` on a `-X`-only class stringifies and fails (0 elements).
  * an overloaded filetest does NOT disturb the `_` cache: probed,
    `stat "/etc/passwd"; -e $ft; stat _` still answers 13.

WHAT DID **NOT** SHIP, and both are filed with their measurements:
  * **#1234** â the STACKED spelling.  perl re-dispatches the handler at EVERY
    level (`-r -e $ft` calls it with "e" then "r" and answers "-r"), and PCL's
    `_`-chain desugaring cannot: a bare `_` after an overloaded test must read
    the PREVIOUS operand (probed) while a stacked op must read the OBJECT.
    54 of op/filetest.t's rows; a COMPILER change.
  * **#1235** â `-t`/`-T`/`-B` on an IO REF run `""` in perl.  PCL cannot tell
    an IO ref from a lexical handle (both are a box holding a stream).  4 rows.

Guard rows 36-44 of `Pl/t/bareword-fh-slot-01.t` (x both emission paths),
inverse-verified against 027ba9c's runtime.
subject: SILENT WRONG (237 companion rows in t/op/filetest.t, the largest unowned family there): a FILETEST does not run its operand's `""` (or `-X`) overload -- `-e $obj` on a string-overloaded object is FALSE in PCL and TRUE in perl, so an existence check silently fails
